inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, held FLAT (SBC expensed in the flows). 267.52M common shares issued at 2026-06-30 (Q2-2026 balance sheet) less 2.673M repurchased for cancellation after quarter-end (Q2-2026 MD&A 'Subsequent event', $176M), = 264.85M, plus ~1.2M in-the-money option dilution (1.5M antidilutive options excluded per note 'Earnings per share') -> 266.0M.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual statement of changes in equity 'Stock-based compensation expense' $60M (MG.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt:8715) plus $5M 'Tax withholdings on vesting of equity awards' (financing, KPI EquityAwardTaxes); no combined figure published, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are US GAAP in USD; MG.TO quotes in CAD on the TSX. Per-share values computed in USD and converted at USD/CAD 1.4254 (Yahoo CAD=X, 2026-10-10T04:21Z). Parity check against the NYSE listing MGA (1:1 same share): US$63.99 x 1.4254 = C$91.21 vs observed C$91.24 (0.03% tie), confirming rate, direction and quote basis.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built WACC. Rf 4.3% (US 10y), beta 1.35 (cyclical Tier-1 supplier), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~11.05%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (investment-grade senior notes), after-tax ~3.9%. Weights at market: equity ~US$17.0bn (266M x US$63.99), debt US$4.6bn (leases excluded, consistent with lease treatment) -> ~79/21 -> WACC ~9.5%. Same WACC in all scenarios: cyclicality is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 12x terminal cap, not as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Magna reports under US GAAP: operating lease cost (~US$0.4bn/yr) is a straight-line operating expense already deducted inside EBITDA and inside OCF, and D&A carries no right-of-use depreciation. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore 0 (no second charge) and the US$1,841M operating lease liability (Q2-2026) is EXCLUDED from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI charged once in the equity bridge at an estimated market value of US$450M (~10x NCI earnings of ~US$45M/yr; book US$342M at 2026-06-30). NCI dividends (~US$60M/yr) are not separately deducted from flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with non-US/cyclical adaptations (routing table row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Magna is a Tier-1 auto supplier: an operating company whose value is free cash flow; not a bank/REIT/holdco. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). CYCLE JUDGMENT: FY2025 reported EBITDA (7.6%) and net margin (2.0%) are depressed by US$736M of 'Other expense, net' (restructuring, impairments, EV-program write-downs) and Q1-2026's net loss is a US$415M Other-expense quarter, not an operating loss (Q1-2026 Adjusted EBIT stayed positive; H1-2026 adjusted after-tax operating profit US$973M). The operating trough is in Adjusted EBIT, 5.4-5.6% in FY2023-25 against 7.6-7.9% in FY2017-18 on far higher European LVP; FY2026 guidance is 6.3-6.6%. The base case runs Adjusted EBIT to ~6.9% mid-cycle, neither the trough nor the 2017-18 peak. ENGINE EBITDA DEFINITION: ebitda_margin_path = Adjusted EBIT + depreciation/amortization ex acquired-intangible amortization (~3.8%) + SBC (~0.18%, added back because the engine charges it separately) - a recurring cash-restructuring haircut of ~0.35% of sales (Other expense has been non-zero in every year FY2016-FY2025; its cash part is a recurring cost of this business, not a one-off). FY2026 path value 10.0% therefore ties to ~6.4% Adjusted EBIT, the guidance midpoint. Equity income (LG Magna e-Powertrain and other JVs, ~US$0.15-0.2bn/yr) sits inside Adjusted EBIT, so the US$1,248M equity-accounted Investments line is NOT added to the bridge (matching-asset rule). CAPEX is fixed-asset additions PLUS 'Increase in investments, other assets and intangible assets' (tooling, capitalized engineering), matching Magna's own FCF definition: FY2025 1,313 + 499 = 1,812 (4.3%); H1-2026 488 + 245. REPORTED FCF FY2025 = OCF 3,598 - 1,313 - 499 = 1,786 (company basis; FY2026 guidance US$1.75-1.85bn). Interest income (US$66M FY2025) is NOT stripped: Magna is a net debtor, the rule applies only to material net cash. BUYBACKS: an active repurchaser (US$905M H1-2026 plus US$176M after quarter-end; US$137M FY2025), so the flat count is funded, not a convention. DIVESTITURES: Lighting and Rooftop Systems (~US$1.1bn 2025 sales) sold during 2026; FY2026 guidance (US$41.3-42.5bn) is net of the part-year effect, and FY2027 growth absorbs the remaining full-year drag. NET DEBT: long-term debt incl. current portion US$4,628M (no short-term borrowings outstanding at 2026-06-30) less cash US$1,430M, with cash reduced by the US$176M post-quarter buyback so cash and share count share one date -> US$3,374M. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables 8.4bn + inventory 4.0bn exceed payables 7.3bn + accruals, so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is negative (-10% of the revenue change).

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at estimated market value
equity_bridge.note: Book US$342M at 2026-06-30 (Q2-2026 balance sheet); NCI income ~US$45M/yr (H1-2026 US$21M) x ~10. Flows are 100%-consolidated, so NCI is charged here once.

equity_bridge.item: Long-term employee benefit liabilities, after tax
equity_bridge.note: US$519M at 2026-06-30 (pension / termination / long-service, mostly Austria/Germany/Canada) x (1 - ~25%). Debt-like; not in net debt.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (1.9%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr (5.2%) and EPS 3yr (13.0%). Equity is held down by ~US$5.0bn of buybacks FY2020-H1 2026 and FY2022/FY2025 impairments, so it understates the business's growth; revenue 5yr starts from the FY2020 COVID trough and overstates it. The forward base path is anchored on FY2026 guidance and light-vehicle-production (LVP) plus content growth (~2.5-3.5%), not on any one CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs here use Metrics FCF (OCF - fixed-asset additions) less SBC and equity-award taxes. Both are endpoint artefacts: 3yr starts at the FY2022 trough (owner FCF ~US$368M, working-capital build plus chip-shortage margins) and 5yr starts at FY2020's COVID working-capital release. Owner-FCF CAGR sits below the reported CAGR only marginally; SBC is ~0.15% of sales, so the gap is immaterial. EPS 3yr starts from the depressed FY2022 base (US$2.03).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = guidance midpoint US$41.9bn (net of Lighting/Rooftop part-year exit). FY2027 +1.5%: remaining divestiture drag (~-1.3%) against flat LVP and +2-3% growth-over-market from launches. FY2028-31 3-3.5%: modest European/N. American LVP recovery plus ADAS/electrification content. Fades to 2% nominal.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: 10.0% ties to ~6.4% Adjusted EBIT (guide 6.3-6.6%). Steps to 10.5% (~6.9% Adjusted EBIT) by FY2029 on MAFACT/'Most Impactful Divisions' cost actions and Power & Vision mix; mid-cycle, below the 7.6-7.9% of FY2017-18.
base.capex_rationale: Fixed + other-asset/tooling investment. FY2026 ~3.8% on H1 run-rate; normalizes to 4.2% (D&A 3.95% plus modest growth capex). FY2023-24 launch peak was 6.5-7.0% incl. other assets; FY2025 4.3%.

bull.ebitda_margin_rationale: Adjusted EBIT recovers to ~7.9%, the FY2017-18 level, on European volume recovery, ADAS/eDrive mix and completed portfolio pruning.

bear.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2027 LVP downturn (USMCA/tariff shock, N. American EV cancellations) takes Adjusted EBIT to ~4.6%, a FY2022-type year; mid-cycle settles at ~5.4%, i.e. the FY2023-25 trough becomes the norm as Chinese OEMs take share from Magna's legacy customers.

scenario_narratives.base: Magna delivers its raised FY2026 guide (sales ~US$41.9bn, Adjusted EBIT ~6.4%, FCF ~US$1.8bn), absorbs the Lighting/Rooftop exit in FY2027, and grows 3-3.5% for a few years as European and North American light-vehicle production edges off its lows and ADAS/eDrive content outgrows the market by 1-3pp. Cost programs (MAFACT, 'Most Impactful Divisions') lift Adjusted EBIT to ~6.9%, mid-cycle rather than the 2017-18 peak; restructuring keeps recurring at ~0.35% of sales. Tariffs stay largely recovered from OEMs; USMCA stays in annual review without a rupture.
scenario_narratives.bull: European volumes recover toward pre-COVID levels, the Chery/XPENG/GAC wins become a real Chinese-OEM channel, and Power & Vision's ADAS/electrification mix keeps compounding, so sales grow 4-5% and Adjusted EBIT returns to ~7.9% (FY2017-18). EV-program recoveries from GM/Ford are fully collected, buybacks keep shrinking the count, and the November 2026 investor day adds an adjacent-market (robotics/automation) option the base gives no credit for.
scenario_narratives.bear: A North American volume shock (USMCA non-renewal path, Section 232 tariffs hitting affordability) plus more Detroit EV-program cancellations cut sales ~5% in FY2027 and take Adjusted EBIT to a FY2022-type ~4.6%. Chinese OEMs keep taking share from GM, Mercedes, BMW, VW and Stellantis faster than Magna can win COEM work, so mid-cycle margins settle at ~5.4%, i.e. the FY2023-25 trough becomes the norm, and capex intensity stays high to defend programs.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default: six OEMs take most of sales, USMCA entered annual review on 2026-07-01, and tariff and EV-program decisions are outside Magna's control, so a volume-led downturn is a live path, not a tail. Base 50%: it sits on raised FY2026 guidance and a mid-cycle margin the company has delivered before. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs European volume recovery AND a return to peak-era margins AND Chinese-OEM traction, which are three separate things that all have to go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Magna on mid-cycle owner cash flow, not on the FY2025 reported trough (2.0% net margin, depressed by US$736M of Other expense) and not on the FY2017-18 peak. Recurring restructuring is charged as a cost, the cyclicality sits in the probability-weighted flows and a 12x terminal cap, and the WACC carries no extra premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: The terminal value is capped at 12x FCF in every scenario (Gordon at 9.5%/2% would be ~13.6x), so the value is sensitive to the cap multiple a cyclical supplier can command
Customer concentration (GM, Mercedes-Benz, Ford, BMW, VW, Stellantis) and Chinese-OEM share gains
USMCA annual review and Section 232/IEEPA tariff regime changes
Recurring 'Other expense' (restructuring/impairments) running above the 0.35%-of-sales haircut
USD/CAD moves change the CAD value one-for-one; the rate is static between refreshes
